The major disadvantage with torson helical gear type diffs is if one tire lifts or is on ice, no torque can be transferred to the other tractive tire. Gear teeth angle and friction determines the torque bias ratio.

The Torsen differential works just like a conventional differential, but can lock up if a torque imbalance occurs, the maximum ratio of torque imbalance being defined by the Torque Bias Ratio (TBR). When a Torsen has a 3:1 TBR, that means that one side of the differential can handle up to 75% while the other side would have to only handle 25% of applied torque. During acceleration under asymmetric traction conditions, so long as the higher traction side can handle the higher percentage of applied torque, no relative wheelspin will occur. When the traction difference exceeds the TBR, the slower output side of the differential receives the tractive torque of the faster wheel multiplied by the TBR; any extra torque remaining from applied torque contributes to the angular acceleration of the faster output side of the differential.

It's in the math, 0 multiplied by any number always equals 0. 0 torque at the low traction tire results in 0 torque transferred to the high traction tire.

Traction control is also different. It is first and foremost a throttle limiter to hold back available power. Then even if that's too much it will use the ABS system in reverse to stop wheel spin. As in reverse I mean that ABS first and foremost function is to prevent wheel lock-up.

That's virtually every modern ABS system I've seen, they go hand in hand (though traction control generally also includes an electronic throttle and extra control over the transmission). A typical four channel system consists of:

-1 pump to control - activate to pressurize accumulators

-4 valves to direct pressurized fluid to the lines - activate to apply breaks

-4 valves to direct the lines to reservoir - activate to release breaks

Accurately controlling the pressure can't really be done with PWM due to the high pressure of the system and slow response time of the hydraulic solenoids (think 100ms or more).
